subject.title: [Bug]: Teams app removal/re-add retains prior DM session history

question: For true Microsoft Teams app-management remove or uninstall lifecycle events, should OpenClaw stale the routed session and remove the cached proactive conversation reference without deleting transcript data?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the fix chooses a privacy and retained-history boundary for Teams personal chats after app removal, which automation should not decide alone.

options.title: Stale session and clear cached reference
options.body: Use the existing non-destructive session-boundary pattern, clear the Teams proactive conversation reference, and preserve transcript files unless a separate retention policy says otherwise.

options.title: Stale only the routed session
options.body: Limit the fix to context isolation while accepting cached proactive conversation references as a separate follow-up risk.

options.title: Delete retained Teams data
options.body: Treat app removal as a destructive retention boundary, which needs explicit data-loss policy, migration behavior, and stronger security review.

recommendation.title: Stale session and clear cached reference
recommendation.body: Use the existing non-destructive session-boundary pattern, clear the Teams proactive conversation reference, and preserve transcript files unless a separate retention policy says otherwise.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Teams state-store and security-sensitive channel history makes this the best available owner for the retention-boundary choice.
